title: Axis ticks with an int counter

blocks.text: A `double` used as a loop counter collects rounding error: adding `0.1` ten times gives `0.9999999999999999`, not `1.0`. Drive the loop with an `int` counter and compute each value from it instead.
Write `ticks(double start, double step, int count)` in `Ticks`. It returns `count` values, where value `i` is `start + i * step`:

cases.says: ticks(0.0, 0.1, 11) ends with exactly 1.0: no error is accumulated.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A floating-point loop counter accumulates rounding error, so an int counter drives the loop instead.
